1	# andesim-demo
2	
3	Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
4	every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
5	(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).
6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
10	  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
11	- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).
12	
13	## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`
14	
15	Fill in these settings if your paths differ:
16	
17	```Makefile
18	ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
19	TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
20	ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
21	```
22	
23	## Step 2: Build
24	
25	```bash
26	make
27	```
28	
29	Each demo links against the andesim runtime
30	(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
31	runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.
32	
33	## Step 3: Run
34	
35	Run every mode of one demo:
36	
37	```bash
38	make run-hello
39	make run-lm
40	make run-lm_slave
41	make run-lm_dma
42	make run-hvm_slave
43	make run-hvm_dma
44	make run-rvv
45	make run-fp
46	make run-cache
47	make run-verify
48	make run-syscall
49	make run-coremark
50	make run-dhrystone
51	make run-cpp
52	```
53	
54	Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
55	`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `fp-*`, `cache-*`, `verify-*`,
56	`syscall-*`, `coremark-*`, `dhrystone-*` and `cpp-*` targets work the
57	same way):
58	
59	| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
60	|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
61	| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
62	| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
63	| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
64	| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |
65	
66	`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
67	QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
68	small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
69	outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
70	checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
71	On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
72	the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.
73	
74	`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
75	SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
76	DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
77	slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
78	(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
79	memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
80	engines and the content crossed the handoff.
81	
82	`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
83	controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
84	aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
85	ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
86	That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
87	models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
88	bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.
89	
90	The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
91	vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
92	enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
93	its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
94	demo:
95	
96	- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
97	  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
98	  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
99	  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
100	  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
101	- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
102	  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
103	  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.
104	
105	On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
106	each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
107	256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.
108	
109	`demo/rvv` tests the vector unit: the ROI runs an RVV-intrinsic kernel
110	(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works); the
111	workload is an 8x8x8 int32 GEMM. The QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar
112	reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector unit and
113	compares. `RVV_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after the
114	handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
115	`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
116	is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
117	vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
118	accepts it.
119	
120	`demo/fp` covers the scalar FPU's state, `fcsr`, the way `demo/rvv`
121	covers the vector unit. The QEMU phase clears `fflags`, sets the
122	rounding mode to RTZ (the reset default is RNE) and raises the sticky
123	divide-by-zero flag with a real `1.0f/0.0f`; the vsim ROI computes
124	`1.0f/3.0f` -- a quotient that rounds DIFFERENTLY under RTZ
125	(`0x3eaaaaaa`) and RNE (`0x3eaaaaab`) -- then reads the CSRs back.
126	`FP_OK` means the transported `frm` steered a real divide after the
127	handoff (not just a CSR readback), the pre-handoff DZ flag is still
128	sticky, and the divide's own NX landed on top of it: `fcsr` crossed
129	intact.
130	
131	`demo/cache` prices the config transport: the SAME kernel (4 passes
132	over a 1 KB volatile array) in two hybrid builds. `cache_on` is the
133	untouched program -- crt0 enables the L1 caches at boot, and only the
134	transported `mcache_ctl` makes the vsim ROI run cached, as this
135	program would on silicon. `cache_off` clears the IC|DC enable bits
136	before the ROI, so the transported value disables the caches and the
137	same window runs uncached -- about 4.5k vs 42.5k cycles, a ~9x gap on
138	this kernel (`make check-cache` asserts ratio > 2x). Without the
139	transport EVERY hybrid figure would look like `cache_off`: the engine
140	resets with caches off. The demo also carries the platform-cache MMIO
141	transport tests (`l2c.elf`/`l3c.elf`, one source): the program stages
142	patterns in the shared-cache registers (Control policy bits, HPM
143	Control, way masks) on the QEMU leg and asserts them back FROM THE RTL
144	inside the ROI, printing `L2C_OK`/`L3C_OK`. Hybrid-only by design, and
145	engine-gated: check.sh picks the leg matching the engine's CACHE
146	column (`L2:*` on 45-series, `L3:*` on 46/66) and SKIPs, naming the
147	RTL config, when it shows `-`. There is no cache_off cycle target on
148	purpose: disabling the D-cache mid-run on the RTL would strand its
149	dirty lines (that needs a CCTL flush first); on hybrid the vsim
150	caches start empty at the restore, so the plain disable is exact.
151	
152	`demo/verify` is about trusting the figure: `make verify-hybrid-marker`
153	runs a state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP under RTZ, an RVV
154	loop, CSR writes before and inside the ROI) with `--verify`, which
155	re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI exit and compares the
156	drained state field by field against the cycle engine
157	(`[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS`). The demo also shows the
158	failing side: `make verify-taint-hybrid-marker` runs a build whose only
159	difference is one instruction -- an `mcycle` sample into `t6` right at
160	the exit marker. The engines count cycles differently by design, so
161	that register cannot match: verify exits non-zero and the diff names
162	exactly `x31`. `make check-verify` asserts both directions.
163	
164	`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
165	binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
166	host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
167	and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
168	time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
169	runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
170	`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
171	also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
172	file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
173	files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
174	the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
175	hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
176	main's return value through SimControl).
177	
178	`demo/coremark` runs a real benchmark, EEMBC CoreMark, with the EEMBC
179	sources untouched: the ROI markers live in the port layer
180	(`core_portme.c`), inside `start_time()` and `stop_time()` -- the two
181	functions that already delimit the timed run -- so the hybrid window is
182	exactly the region CoreMark times itself with its own `mcycle` reads.
183	That makes the modes cross-check each other: cycle mode's self-reported
184	`Total ticks` and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
185	same region and agree within ~0.5% (the hybrid window starts with cold
186	caches and includes the marker/call boundary). The pc-trigger variant
187	gets the same window from the symbols alone
188	(`--pc-start start_time --pc-end stop_time`). On hybrid the run ends at
189	`stop_time()`'s exit marker, so CoreMark's report (CRCs, validation)
190	prints on fast and cycle only; the hybrid output is just the cycle
191	figure. `ITERATIONS=1` by default -- the CRCs still validate, and each
192	extra iteration adds RTL simulation time.
193	
194	`demo/dhrystone` applies the same recipe to Dhrystone 2.2a (the vsim
195	port, which times with `mcycle`/`minstret` instead of UNIX time APIs):
196	the counter reads moved into `start_time()`/`stop_time()`, which carry
197	the ROI markers outside the reads and double as the
198	`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbols. The guest's self-reported `CycleCnt`
199	(cycle mode) and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
200	same region; on hybrid the run ends at `stop_time()`'s marker, so the
201	`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
202	default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
203	Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
204	second pass with `-DPASS2`).
205	
206	`demo/cpp` proves the runtime's C++ support end to end (g++ through
207	the same two-flag link; `CXX` in `Make.var`). A static object's
208	constructor -- run by crt0's `.init_array` walk BEFORE main --
209	assembles the "CPP" tag one character at a time into a `std::string`;
210	the vsim ROI re-checks that tag from the RTL side (the object's bytes
211	crossed the handoff in the shared mmap), grows a `std::vector` on the
212	newlib heap and composes the `CPP_OK` pass string at runtime, printed
213	inside the ROI. On fast and cycle the run also proves
214	return-from-main == `exit(rc)`: the static destructor prints
215	`CPP_DTOR_OK` after main returns, and main's status rides SimControl.
216	It uses printf, not iostream -- iostreams add static-init and code
217	size that stretch a cycle-mode boot for no extra proof. The pc
218	variant names the window with `--pc-start cpp_roi --pc-end
219	cpp_roi_end`; the kernel is `extern "C"` because the pc trigger
220	resolves symbols by name, so it must stay unmangled. The runtime side
221	(crt0 `.init_array` walk, `andesim.ld` array bounds, crtbegin/crtend
222	in the specs, exit-at-return) landed in the andesim repo on
223	2026-07-15, guarded there by `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh`.
224	
225	Expected output (hybrid):
226	
227	```
228	hello from andesim!
229	[andesim] 3532 cycles
230	```
231	
232	The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
233	close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

237	Every `cycle` and `hybrid` target takes its engine from the `ENGINE`
238	variable (default in `Make.var`), so any demo runs on any engine that
239	`andesim list engines` reports -- the binaries are engine-portable:

241	```bash
242	make hello-hybrid-marker ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced
243	make check ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced        # the whole suite, one engine

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-rvv
make run-fp
make run-cache
make run-verify
make run-syscall
make run-coremark
make run-dhrystone
make run-cpp
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `fp-*`, `cache-*`, `verify-*`,
`syscall-*`, `coremark-*`, `dhrystone-*` and `cpp-*` targets work the
same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/rvv` tests the vector unit: the ROI runs an RVV-intrinsic kernel
(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works); the
workload is an 8x8x8 int32 GEMM. The QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar
reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector unit and
compares. `RVV_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after the
handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

`demo/fp` covers the scalar FPU's state, `fcsr`, the way `demo/rvv`
covers the vector unit. The QEMU phase clears `fflags`, sets the
rounding mode to RTZ (the reset default is RNE) and raises the sticky
divide-by-zero flag with a real `1.0f/0.0f`; the vsim ROI computes
`1.0f/3.0f` -- a quotient that rounds DIFFERENTLY under RTZ
(`0x3eaaaaaa`) and RNE (`0x3eaaaaab`) -- then reads the CSRs back.
`FP_OK` means the transported `frm` steered a real divide after the
handoff (not just a CSR readback), the pre-handoff DZ flag is still
sticky, and the divide's own NX landed on top of it: `fcsr` crossed
intact.

`demo/cache` prices the config transport: the SAME kernel (4 passes
over a 1 KB volatile array) in two hybrid builds. `cache_on` is the
untouched program -- crt0 enables the L1 caches at boot, and only the
transported `mcache_ctl` makes the vsim ROI run cached, as this
program would on silicon. `cache_off` clears the IC|DC enable bits
before the ROI, so the transported value disables the caches and the
same window runs uncached -- about 4.5k vs 42.5k cycles, a ~9x gap on
this kernel (`make check-cache` asserts ratio > 2x). Without the
transport EVERY hybrid figure would look like `cache_off`: the engine
resets with caches off. The demo also carries the platform-cache MMIO
transport tests (`l2c.elf`/`l3c.elf`, one source): the program stages
patterns in the shared-cache registers (Control policy bits, HPM
Control, way masks) on the QEMU leg and asserts them back FROM THE RTL
inside the ROI, printing `L2C_OK`/`L3C_OK`. Hybrid-only by design, and
engine-gated: check.sh picks the leg matching the engine's CACHE
column (`L2:*` on 45-series, `L3:*` on 46/66) and SKIPs, naming the
RTL config, when it shows `-`. There is no cache_off cycle target on
purpose: disabling the D-cache mid-run on the RTL would strand its
dirty lines (that needs a CCTL flush first); on hybrid the vsim
caches start empty at the restore, so the plain disable is exact.

`demo/verify` is about trusting the figure: `make verify-hybrid-marker`
runs a state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP under RTZ, an RVV
loop, CSR writes before and inside the ROI) with `--verify`, which
re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI exit and compares the
drained state field by field against the cycle engine
(`[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS`). The demo also shows the
failing side: `make verify-taint-hybrid-marker` runs a build whose only
difference is one instruction -- an `mcycle` sample into `t6` right at
the exit marker. The engines count cycles differently by design, so
that register cannot match: verify exits non-zero and the diff names
exactly `x31`. `make check-verify` asserts both directions.

`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
main's return value through SimControl).

`demo/coremark` runs a real benchmark, EEMBC CoreMark, with the EEMBC
sources untouched: the ROI markers live in the port layer
(`core_portme.c`), inside `start_time()` and `stop_time()` -- the two
functions that already delimit the timed run -- so the hybrid window is
exactly the region CoreMark times itself with its own `mcycle` reads.
That makes the modes cross-check each other: cycle mode's self-reported
`Total ticks` and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region and agree within ~0.5% (the hybrid window starts with cold
caches and includes the marker/call boundary). The pc-trigger variant
gets the same window from the symbols alone
(`--pc-start start_time --pc-end stop_time`). On hybrid the run ends at
`stop_time()`'s exit marker, so CoreMark's report (CRCs, validation)
prints on fast and cycle only; the hybrid output is just the cycle
figure. `ITERATIONS=1` by default -- the CRCs still validate, and each
extra iteration adds RTL simulation time.

`demo/dhrystone` applies the same recipe to Dhrystone 2.2a (the vsim
port, which times with `mcycle`/`minstret` instead of UNIX time APIs):
the counter reads moved into `start_time()`/`stop_time()`, which carry
the ROI markers outside the reads and double as the
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbols. The guest's self-reported `CycleCnt`
(cycle mode) and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region; on hybrid the run ends at `stop_time()`'s marker, so the
`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
second pass with `-DPASS2`).

`demo/cpp` proves the runtime's C++ support end to end (g++ through
the same two-flag link; `CXX` in `Make.var`). A static object's
constructor -- run by crt0's `.init_array` walk BEFORE main --
assembles the "CPP" tag one character at a time into a `std::string`;
the vsim ROI re-checks that tag from the RTL side (the object's bytes
crossed the handoff in the shared mmap), grows a `std::vector` on the
newlib heap and composes the `CPP_OK` pass string at runtime, printed
inside the ROI. On fast and cycle the run also proves
return-from-main == `exit(rc)`: the static destructor prints
`CPP_DTOR_OK` after main returns, and main's status rides SimControl.
It uses printf, not iostream -- iostreams add static-init and code
size that stretch a cycle-mode boot for no extra proof. The pc
variant names the window with `--pc-start cpp_roi --pc-end
cpp_roi_end`; the kernel is `extern "C"` because the pc trigger
resolves symbols by name, so it must stay unmangled. The runtime side
(crt0 `.init_array` walk, `andesim.ld` array bounds, crtbegin/crtend
in the specs, exit-at-return) landed in the andesim repo on
2026-07-15, guarded there by `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh`.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Switching engines

Every `cycle` and `hybrid` target takes its engine from the `ENGINE`
variable (default in `Make.var`), so any demo runs on any engine that
`andesim list engines` reports -- the binaries are engine-portable:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced
make check ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced        # the whole suite, one engine
make check-all-engines                          # the whole suite, EVERY vsim engine
```

`check-all-engines` parses the engine set from `andesim list engines`
at run time (nothing hardcoded; restrict it with
`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b"`) and prints a per-engine summary.
Demos are capability-gated per engine: the local-memory demos
(`lm*`, `hvm*`) are skipped on an engine whose resolved plan carries
no ILM/DLM/HVM, and `rvv` is skipped on an engine without a vector
unit. The gate keys off the engine's `--describe` output, which
advertises LM *transport* (backdoor load + dump in the vsim CPU
wrapper) -- not whether the RTL config has the memories.

### Demo x engine matrix (sweep of 2026-07-14)

| Demo      | vsim:ax45mpv_premium | vsim:ax46mpv_advanced | vsim:ax66_makatau | Blocking layer for SKIP/FAIL |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|
| hello     | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| lm        | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
| lm_slave  | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
| lm_dma    | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
| hvm_slave | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no HVM |
| hvm_dma   | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no HVM |
| rvv       | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| fp        | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| cache     | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| cache/l2c+l3c | SKIP | SKIP | PASS (L3C) | RTL: ax45/ax46 built with `NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` (no shared-cache block); wrapper+driver transport ready |
| verify    | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| syscall   | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| coremark  | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| dhrystone | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| memsize   | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| cpp       | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |

The cpp row is from the 2026-07-15 run, the day the runtime's C++
support landed (andesim commit `946e2e3`): all four legs (fast, cycle,
hybrid marker + pc) pass on all three engines; no capability gate --
C++ needs nothing engine-specific.

The cache/l2c+l3c row is the platform-cache MMIO transport leg inside
`make check-cache` (sweep of 2026-07-15). The shared cache is the L2C
on 45-series engines and the L3C on 46/66-series -- separate tests,
same registers: `l3c.elf` passes on ax66_makatau's live 512K L3C
(`andesim list engines` CACHE column `L3:512K`); ax45mpv_premium and
ax46mpv_advanced are RTL-blocked (size 0 in their engine cfgs, and
their current RTL drops do not support a shared-cache configuration),
so the leg SKIPs there naming that layer. When an RTL drop with the
block arrives, the leg starts running by itself: the gate is
`--describe`-driven, so no wrapper, driver, or demo change is needed.

The ax66 lm*/hvm* SKIPs are RTL-layer, not a wrapper transport gap:
`vsim_andesim/data/configs/ax66_makatau.cfg` sets
`NDS_ILM_SUPPORT no`, `NDS_DLM_SUPPORT no` (sizes 0) and has no HVM
section at all -- `--describe`'s `ilm_size/dlm_size/hvm_size: 0` is
the wrapper reporting that truthfully. (Contrast with the ax46 history
below, where the RTL HAD the memories and the wrapper was the gap.)

demo/syscall FAILED on ax66 in earlier sweeps: the legacy HTIF
protocol staged syscall args/results in cacheable RAM which the vsim
host peeked/poked by backdoor -- invisible through ax66's private
write-back PL2C, so the guest read its own stale line back
(`SYSCALL_STAGE_BAD gettimeofday`). Fixed on 2026-07-14 by moving the
mailbox into an uncached SimControl device window (coherent by
construction on every cache hierarchy; `flush_dcache()` deleted from
the runtime). Contract + evidence: `andesim/ROADMAP_HTIF_WINDOW.md`;
commits vsim_andesim `c90c234`, qemu fork `2342ca8227`, andesim

Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.

Conventions (same as the existing demos):

# Ports from /local/nick/vsim-demo-new (study 2026-07-15)

Entries 12-16 come from a port study of the old vsim demo suite. Same rules:
one session builds ONE entry. The study's "no port needed / not portable"
verdicts are recorded at the bottom so the analysis is not redone.

## 12. atomic

State: TODO
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
Origin: vsim-demo-new `atomic-test`.

LR/SC + AMO contract on every engine - nothing in the suite touches the A
extension today. Four tests in a `noinline` `atomic_kernel()` inside the
ROI: (T1) LR/SC pair succeeds and commits; (T2) after an SC consumes the
reservation, a second SC to the same address must fail and must not write;
(T3) `amoswap.w` returns old, writes new; (T4) 5x `amoadd.w` +7 on 100
== 135. T2 is a deliberate redesign: the source demo broke the reservation
with a same-hart store, which the ISA leaves implementation-defined (QEMU's
value-compare cmpxchg and the RTL monitor may legitimately diverge);
SC-after-SC failure is architecturally guaranteed on both. Every LR/SC pair
stays entirely inside the ROI - a reservation is microarchitectural and
cannot cross the QEMU->vsim handoff. The target variable is a
`static volatile uint32_t` in .bss (plain DRAM). No engine gating: A is
baseline on all three engines.

- Key files: `demo/atomic/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest prints `ATOMIC_OK` from inside the ROI only if all four
  tests pass; exit 0 on fast/cycle.
- Deps: none.

## 13. trap

State: TODO
Modes: fast + cycle only (expected-fail demo; hybrid's pass signal is a
printed marker, and this demo's whole point is the exit-code contract).
Origin: vsim-demo-new `negative_test`.

A faulting guest must fail loudly on every engine. main prints a banner,
then executes an illegal instruction (`.insn r 0x7f, 0, 0, x0, x0, x0`,
fallback `unimp` if engines disagree on mcause). The runtime already does
the rest: `handler.c` prints `[ERROR] Trap occurred! ... mcause: 0x2` and
`_exit(mcause)`, so the driver exits 2. The `run:` target inverts (`!`) so
a correct fault reads as success; `check.sh` (memsize assert helper)
asserts rc==2 AND `Trap occurred` on stderr for both the fast and cycle
legs - loud failure if the guest does NOT trap or the cause differs.

- Key files: `demo/trap/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh green on both legs, on every engine.
- Deps: none.

## 14. cpp

State: DONE (2026-07-15)
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
Origin: vsim-demo-new `cpp`.

C++ on the andesim runtime, unblocked and demoed. Runtime side (andesim
commit `946e2e3`, TDD'd by `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh`, 12/12 vplat
scripts green): crt0 keeps the direct `init_mtvec` call (that name
reference is what extracts handler.o from `libandesim_runtime.a`, and
the trap vector is live before any ctor) then walks `.init_array` via
newlib's `__libc_init_array`; `andesim.ld` PROVIDEs the array bounds
ABOVE `_edata` -- crt0 zeroes `[_edata, _end)` before the walk, so
arrays after `.data` would be wiped; `andesim.specs` adds
crtbegin/crtend (the g++ driver injects `-lstdc++ -lm` itself, so *lib
is untouched); main's return routes through `exit()` (C++
return-from-main == exit(rc): atexit + static dtors run). Demo side:
the static ctor assembles the "CPP" tag into a `std::string` before
main; the vsim ROI re-checks the tag from the RTL (the object's bytes
crossed the handoff), grows a `std::vector` on the newlib heap and
prints the runtime-composed `CPP_OK` inside the ROI; `CPP_DTOR_OK`
prints after main returns (fast/cycle only -- hybrid ends at the exit
marker). The ROI kernel is `extern "C"`: the pc trigger resolves
symbols by name, so `cpp_roi`/`cpp_roi_end` must stay unmangled.
PASS on all four legs x all three engines (see README matrix).

- Key files: `demo/cpp/{main.cpp,Makefile}`, `Make.var` (adds CXX), top
  `Makefile`, `README.md`; andesim `runtime/{crt0.S,handler.c,andesim.ld,
  andesim.specs}` + `tests/fixtures/vplat_cpp.cpp` +
  `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh` + USER_GUIDE 4.1 (other repo).
- Pass: guest prints `CPP_OK` composed by the static ctor inside the
  ROI on every mode; `CPP_DTOR_OK` + exit 0 on fast/cycle.
- Deps: none (runtime change landed).

## 15. smp

State: BLOCKED (no multi-hart engine registered)
Modes: cycle first; hybrid needs driver work.
Origin: vsim-demo-new `smp-test` (spinlock hello, per-hart caches,
shared-cache coherence).

Every registered engine is single-hart (`NDS_NHART=1`). Multi-hart RTL
configs exist (`ax45mpv_mp2`, `ax66_mp2`, NHART=2) but no engine is built
or registered from them. The runtime parks secondary harts
(`CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS=0`; they write 0x01234571 to SimControl and spin),
and the hybrid handoff transports one hart's state. Unblock path: build +
register an mp2 engine, rebuild the runtime with `CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS=1`,
then teach the handoff N harts. The vsim platform already models the SMU
(`smu.hpp`), so the source demo's core-count read (SYSTEMCFG 0xf0100008)
would work. Pairs naturally with the L2C/L3C work from entry 6b.

- Key files: `demo/smp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`;
  engine + runtime + driver work outside this repo.
- Pass: per-hart prints under a spinlock + a shared-cache coherence check.
- Deps: mp2 engine install; CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS runtime; driver handoff.

## 16. irq

State: BLOCKED (vsim platform has no interrupt controllers)
Modes: fast-only today, which is not worth a demo; needs cycle/hybrid.
Origin: vsim-demo-new `platform` (pit/plic/aia interrupt demos).

`vsim_andesim/src/platform/` models only UART, SMU and SimControl - no
PLIC, PLMT or PIT. QEMU's ae350 has andes_plic (0xe4000000) and andes_plmt
(0xe6000000), so an interrupt demo would run on fast but can never run a
cycle or hybrid leg. The source demos also lean on an `INT_TRIGGER`
sim-control backdoor (0xe0080020) that andesim's SimControl does not
provide. Unblock path: model the PLMT first (the machine timer is the
smallest useful interrupt source), then a timer-interrupt-inside-the-ROI
demo; PLIC/external sources later.

- Key files: `demo/irq/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`;
  vsim_andesim platform model work outside this repo.
- Pass: ISR flag set by a timer interrupt taken inside the ROI; `IRQ_OK`.
- Deps: vsim_andesim PLMT (then PLIC) model.

## Port study: no port needed / not portable

Already covered, no port:

- `hello`, `coremark`, `dhrystone`, `rvv`, `syscall` - direct equivalents
  in SUBDIRS (ours add ROI markers, any-VLEN strip-mining, the uncached
  SimControl syscall window).
- `lm_test`, `hvm_test` - covered by `lm`/`lm_slave`/`lm_dma` and
  `hvm_slave`/`hvm_dma`. The old demos filled the memories through a
  sim-control "custom master" backdoor (0xe0080000 = 0xabcdeX); ours use
  the real transports (hart-local view, bus slave aperture, ATCDMAC300).
- `platform/uart_demo` - every demo's printf already exercises UART2.
- `hybrid`, `savable_feat` - the driver's hybrid mode plus the `verify`
  demo ARE the save/restore story; the driver has no user-facing
  `--save`/`--resume`, and adding one is a driver feature, not a demo.

Not portable:

- `ace`, `ace-rvv` - need the COPILOT toolflow (`.eca` for the assembler)
  plus a csim model (`libaceasim.a`) baked into the simulator build, and
  QEMU cannot execute ACE custom instructions, so fast mode, hybrid
  staging and the `--verify` oracle all break by construction. ax66 RTL
  has `NDS_ACE_SUPPORT=no` (ax45/ax46 have `yes`, but the generated
  instructions must match what COPILOT put into the RTL).
- `acervv46quad` - sources missing upstream (its Makefile references
  absent `.ace`/`.c` files and a private GEN_API tool).

  esac

  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?

    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
# (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under $VSIM_BIN_DIR)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
# VSIM_QEMU); empty when setup.sh has not run -- the require below reports it.
VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  fi
